standard_prerequisites: The module E and the square-zero extension ring of the section construction, whose properties (a) through (d) are proved in section prose and restated in the companion lemma lemma-strange-regular-sequence
Over a principal ideal domain a finitely generated torsion-free module is flat; the ring k[z] localized at the prime generated by z is a discrete valuation ring
More on Algebra, Lemma more-algebra-lemma-regular-koszul-regular: a regular sequence is Koszul-regular; hence a pair whose Koszul homology does not vanish cannot be a regular sequence
core_obligations: Set A equal to k[z] localized at the prime generated by z and B equal to the localization of k[x, y, z] plus E at the ideal generated by x, y, z and E; the induced map A to B is a local homomorphism of local rings
Since x, y, z is a regular sequence in B, as shown in the proof of the companion lemma, the pair x, y is a regular sequence in B
B over the ideal generated by x and y is a torsion-free A-module, hence flat over A

On the other hand B over zB carries a nonzero element delta annihilated by the images of x and of y, so the second Koszul homology of the pair of images on B over the maximal ideal of A times B is nonzero
By the Koszul-regular lemma the pair of images is not Koszul-regular, and in particular not a regular sequence
proof_roadmap: Set up the local homomorphism from the section construction
Check flatness of the quotient via torsion-freeness over the discrete valuation ring A
Compute the nonzero Koszul homology class delta and conclude
